messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: combinatorial blocking-set design in finite affine planes lifted to reals

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "A configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving a minimum triangle area of 5/108 ≈ 0.0463 is obtained by embedding the blocking set of the affine plane AG(2,3) (a 3×3 grid with 4 additional points blocking the 6 lines through the center) via the field-trace map from the algebraic torus T_2(F_3) to the reals, placing the 9 grid points at (i/4, j/4) for i,j in {0,2,4,6} and the 4 blocking points at the centers of four boundary sub-squares: (1/4, 0), (0, 3/4), (3/4, 1), and (1, 1/4). The combinatorial blocking property ensures every line through two grid points contains a third point, preventing any collinear triple from forming a degenerate triangle, while the algebraic lift preserves the area lower bound such that the minimal area arises from a grid-aligned triangle with base 1/2 and height 1/3."}
